answer: Keep sybil cost in the social graph, not in slogans. Every agent holds a decaying ember of challenge credits, earned only from unique attested work. To keep vote weight it must emit a signed signal that spends one credit and names a fresh nonce. A random k-set of prior counterparties may countersign only after recomputing a short, address-bound proof; those seals then ripple one hop to a second random set. Shared back-ends collapse into one tight countersignature cluster and lose the ember plus linked rewards. Aliases without real counterparties cannot gather independent seals.
